section_summary: This section follows efforts to counter the belief among some Japanese residents of Brazil that Japan had won the war. It records a proposed Japanese envoy, Allied and Brazilian responses, and the distribution of Japanese newspapers and magazines abroad. The final documents concern a book on Shindo Renmei violence sent to General Douglas MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese newspapers
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Japanese newspapers sent under five departmental instructions.
subfiles.summary: Cross confirms receipt of newspapers enclosed with instructions dated April 9, 1947.

subfiles.title: Instruction to the Political Adviser for Japan, fragment
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: A largely illegible instruction is addressed to the Political Adviser for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Only the addressee and instruction heading are legible.

subfiles.title: Transmission of a Japanese residents' memorandum
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Forwards a supplementary memorial from Japanese leaders in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Cross sends a translated memorandum and S. Furuya's letter to Hitoshi Ashida.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning the São Paulo memorial
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Responds to the consulate's transmission of a Japanese residents' memorial.
subfiles.summary: The damaged instruction acknowledges the despatch and lists another despatch and enclosure.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese newspapers
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Acknowledges additional Japanese newspapers sent by the Department.
subfiles.summary: Cross confirms receipt of newspapers enclosed with instructions issued in April.

subfiles.title: Availability of Japanese news for Jornal Paulista
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese news sources for Hideo Onaga's Jornal Paulista.
subfiles.summary: Onaga seeks Asahi and Mainichi; Cross credits the newspaper with informing São Paulo's Japanese community.

subfiles.title: Reply on supplying Japanese newspapers
subfiles.about: Discusses practical limits on obtaining Tokyo newspapers for local distribution.
subfiles.summary: Shipping difficulties restrict the Department to single copies of newspapers; the consulate may seek another source.

subfiles.title: Reply to Pedro Moroni's publication request
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Responds to an inquiry about importing Japanese publications for sale in São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: The Department sees no present means for Moroni to import the publications into Brazil.

subfiles.title: Request to purchase Japanese-language publications
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Seeks a way for Pedro Moroni to import Japanese books and magazines.
subfiles.summary: Cross endorses Moroni's proposed publications as useful to Japanese readers in São Paulo state.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government proposal to send an envoy to Brazil
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese proposal to send an envoy to address unrest among Japanese residents of Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards the Japanese request and says Allied headquarters is considering it.

subfiles.title: Request to dispatch an envoy to Brazil
subfiles.from: K. Asakai, Central Liaison Office, Tokyo
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests approval for a Japanese envoy to speak with residents in Brazil who deny Japan's surrender.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recounts violence, unsuccessful messages from Japan, and requests from residents for a respected visitor. It proposes a one-month stay under Allied and Brazilian conditions.

subfiles.title: Decision on proposed Japanese envoy
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports that no further action will be taken on Japan's proposed envoy.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards Allied staff views and a Swedish note stating Brazil considers an envoy unnecessary.

subfiles.title: G-1 objections to a Japanese envoy
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Argues against allowing a Japanese Government envoy to travel to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: G-1 cites Brazilian jurisdiction and doubts an acceptable Japanese public figure could persuade committed victory believers.

subfiles.title: Government Section objections to a Japanese envoy
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Opposes the envoy as inconsistent with occupation travel and diplomatic policy.
subfiles.summary: The section warns that the visit would breach Allied restrictions and intrude on Brazilian affairs.

subfiles.title: Swedish note on Brazil's response to the envoy proposal
subfiles.about: Conveys Brazil's view that an envoy is no longer needed.
subfiles.summary: Brazil thanks Japan for the offer but says calmer conditions permit Brazilian authorities to handle the unrest.

subfiles.title: Airgram on continued victory propaganda
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Discusses continuing Japanese victory propaganda and the value of newspapers.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text says nationalist intimidation persists and newspapers requested in despatch No. 57 would help.

subfiles.title: Attitude and activities of Japanese residents in Brazil
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports continuing unrest and a Japanese request to mail newspapers overseas.
subfiles.summary: The despatch forwards an intelligence article and notes Japan's request to send 140 daily newspaper copies abroad.

subfiles.title: Reaction of Japanese in the Americas
subfiles.about: Analyzes beliefs in Japanese victory and related intimidation across the Americas.
subfiles.summary: Based on intercepted mail, the article describes Shindo Renmei propaganda, killings of Japanese who accepted defeat, fraud, and demands for reliable news from Japan. It also reports smaller victory-believer groups in Peru, Hawaii, Mexico, Cuba, Sweden, and the United States.

subfiles.title: BA assessment of Japanese residents in Brazil
subfiles.about: Assesses current unrest and possible shipment of Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Dawson reports tranquility and favors distributing newspapers through regular mail or steamer pouch.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 44 on newspapers for Japanese residents
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Urges consideration of Japan's request to mail newspapers to residents of several American countries.
subfiles.summary: The Department relays Cross's view that newspapers would weaken nationalist groups still active in Brazil.

subfiles.title: Consular assessment of Japanese residents in Brazil
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Assesses improved conditions and recommends wider newspaper circulation.
subfiles.summary: Cross credits letters and newspapers with improvement but says nationalist groups persist; Brazilian authorities oppose a delegation.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese victory propaganda
subfiles.about: Requests a current assessment and advice on distributing Japanese newspapers.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks whether nationalist propaganda persists and whether additional newspapers would help counter it.

subfiles.title: São Paulo airgram on continuing nationalist activity
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Reports that victory propaganda still troubles Japanese residents.
subfiles.summary: Cross says murders have ceased but nationalist activity continues; Japanese newspapers would be valuable.

subfiles.title: Return of documents to NA files
subfiles.about: Returns attached documents believed to belong in NA files.
subfiles.summary: Gosho returns attached documents for filing.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on the Sebald despatch
subfiles.about: Summarizes the intelligence article and suggests seeking regional comment on newspaper distribution.
subfiles.summary: The note summarizes victory beliefs in Brazil and proposes consulting American Republic Affairs about Japanese newspapers.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to arrange a steady newspaper supply
subfiles.about: Recommends arrangements to send Japanese newspapers regularly to São Paulo.
subfiles.summary: Clark cites Cross's concern and proposes coordinating supply with occupation authorities and local distribution.

subfiles.title: Civil Censorship highlights for June
subfiles.about: Summarizes censorship findings on Japanese victory beliefs and political attitudes.
subfiles.summary: Green reports persistent Shindo influence in Brazil and smaller extremist groups elsewhere, then suggests checking whether newspapers are being sent. The memorandum also summarizes intercepted Japanese views of the Ashida Government.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 112 requesting newspaper shipment status
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Requests the status of Japan's plan to send newspapers to residents abroad.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites continued victory beliefs and nationalist influence in Brazil.

subfiles.title: Japanese publications being sent abroad
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports quantities and recipients of Japanese publications sent overseas.
subfiles.summary: Enclosed tables show distribution before and after an August reduction caused by higher prices and limited funds.

subfiles.title: Publication shipments, April through July 1948
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese newspapers and magazines sent to overseas destinations from April through July.
subfiles.summary: The table gives destination counts for Asahi, Mainichi, and five magazines.

subfiles.title: Publication shipments after August 1, 1948
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists reduced Japanese newspaper and magazine shipments after August 1.
subfiles.summary: The table gives destination counts for Asahi, Mainichi, Chuo-Koron, and Sekai no Ugoki.

subfiles.title: Destinations of Japanese newspapers and magazines
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Names people and organizations receiving Japanese publications abroad.
subfiles.summary: Recipients span South and North America, Hawaii, and China.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Shindo Renmei book
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Sends two copies of Mario Botelho de Miranda's book on Shindo Renmei.
subfiles.summary: Cross asks that the author's autographed copy be forwarded to General MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for São Paulo despatch
subfiles.about: Designates a copy of São Paulo despatch No. 344 as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: The form says the original action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: Copy of despatch transmitting Shindo Renmei book
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Repeats the request to forward Miranda's autographed book to General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Only the damaged closing portion of the replacement copy is legible.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 184 forwarding Shindo Renmei
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Miranda's book under separate cover for General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: The brief instruction identifies the book and its intended recipient.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on MacArthur's acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Suggests relaying MacArthur's thanks to the book's author.
subfiles.summary: Schuler proposes asking the cultural officer in Rio to convey MacArthur's appreciation to Miranda.

subfiles.title: Delivery of Shindo Renmei to General MacArthur
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Confirms delivery of Miranda's autographed book to General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur asks the Department to convey his appreciation, regards, and good wishes to Miranda.

subfiles.title: Instruction to convey MacArthur's thanks
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Requests that General MacArthur's thanks be conveyed to Mario Botelho de Miranda.
subfiles.summary: The consular officer may relay MacArthur's appreciation, cordial regards, and good wishes.
